arange.shape_layout: Always a newly allocated 1-D ndarray (including length zero), native C-contiguous storage; no axis/order/out/endpoint argument. An explicit non-native-endian dtype is computed in a native descriptor then byteswapped and restored.

dtype.inference: Start from npy_intp descriptor and combine input descriptors; Python integer-only native ranges infer at least npy_intp, real/complex/object follow input discovery; not linspace's ensure-inexact rule.
dtype.legal_numeric: Native bool/int/uint/float/complex with legacy fill slot, object dtype with object arithmetic, and datetime/timedelta special path. Bool is legal only for length<=2; lengths>2 fail TypeError via BOOL_fill.
dtype.rejected: DTypes lacking legacy fill slot, including tested fixed strings/unicode and subarray dtype; TypeError even where an empty result might otherwise look harmless.
dtype.float16: HALF_fill converts stored first two half values to float32, calculates float32 delta and start+i*delta, then rounds to half. This is reference behavior, not proof of Atlas native-precision architectural compliance.

operational_contract: Normalize omitted/None step to 1, omitted/None stop to original start with start=0.

Compute q=(stop-start)/step using Python numeric operations; length=max(ceil(q),0) after checked conversion to npy_intp. Nonzero numerator whose quotient underflows to signed zero produces length0 for negative zero and length1 for positive zero.
When dtype is complex and q is a Python complex object, length uses min(ceil(real(q)),ceil(imag(q))) rather than silently imposing real-only bounds.

Write cast(start) and, when length>=2, cast(start+step); for length>2 invoke dtype fill using effective delta cast(start+step)-cast(start). Do not replace with start+i*user_step or assume stop is never passed after rounding.

For object dtype the fill loop performs Python subtract/add; user exceptions propagate. For integer overflow and reduced-precision rounding, retain dtype-specific source semantics rather than Python arbitrary-precision range semantics.

datetime_contract.dispatch: Datetime/timedelta dtype or inputs route to datetime_arange before general descriptor/fill processing.
datetime_contract.rules: Infer or honor explicit time-unit metadata; datetime ranges require start and stop, datetime cannot be step; integer/timedelta stop with datetime start denotes duration added to start. datetime_contract.length: Signed integer ceiling formula with directional empty range; reject NaT in any input and reject step=0. Calendar/nonlinear units remain datetime metadata conversion semantics.

linspace.value_contract: num is operator.index-compatible and >=0. Set D=num-1 if endpoint else num. For endpoint and num>1, overwrite final sample with stop. num0 gives empty samples and NaN step; num1 with endpointTrue gives start and NaN step; num1 with endpointFalse gives start and step=stop-start. retstepTrue returns (samples,step).

If dtypeNone, output dtype=dt; else normalize requested descriptor, but work remains dt and final cast follows logspace's behavior, with no floor-for-integer rule. geomspace.value_contract: Before num validation, reject if any start or stop equals zero, even if num=0. Cast/copy endpoints to dt. Let s=sign(start), a=start/s, b=stop/s. Compute logspace(log10(a),log10(b),num,endpoint,base=10,dtype=dt); when num>0 overwrite first value with a, and when endpoint and num>1 overwrite last with b; multiply by s, move sample axis, cast output. Endpoints match after the prescribed operations/cast, not an assumed exact-integer interior progression.
geomspace.real_complex_legal_cases: Nonzero same-sign real endpoints permit increasing/decreasing positive or negative progressions. Opposite-sign real endpoints are not rejected: real logarithm yields invalid interior values (warnings/NaNs or seterr errors), with endpoint patches preserved. Complex inputs/dtype follow the rotated principal logarithmic branch and shortest-phase path; branch cuts/signed zero require phase-sensitive tests. NaN/Inf are not blanket-rejected.
